messages:
acme-rep: Hey team — we've got a customer (FinApps Inc) saying their assistant got noticeably more 'to-the-point' after the model bump yesterday. They say helpful context and softening language disappeared. Can we triage?

sofia.chen: Thanks for flagging. Which model/version did they see? Any samples?

acme-rep: They call the API from our hosted endpoint. They say it was fine on redwood-v8.3, changed after redwood-v9.0 canary rolled yesterday afternoon. Sample prompt they sent:  ```
User: "How do I rotate API keys for our service without causing downtime?"
```

acme-rep: Expected (previous behavior):
```
Assistant: Rotating API keys can be done with minimal downtime by following these steps: 1) Create a new key and add it to your config, 2) deploy a short-lived feature flag to accept both keys, 3) roll traffic to the new key, 4) revoke the old key after verification. Make sure to monitor auth errors and have a rollback plan. Would you like an example script?
```

acme-rep: Observed (post-bump):
```
Assistant: Create new key, deploy it alongside old key, switch traffic, revoke old key.
```

mike_g: Hmm, that is a big drop in elaboration. Do they include API call params (temperature, max_tokens, top_p)?

acme-rep: Yes — they set temperature=0.1 and max_tokens=120. Calls were to /v1/generate with model="redwood-v9.0" and role=system: "You are a friendly assistant."

kai-h: deploy-bot shows: 
"deploy-bot: redwood-v9.0 canary -> 10% traffic at 2024-11-12T18:34:00Z"

deploy-bot: redwood-v9.0 canary roll: started by @releases.

ellie_support: Can you ask customer for a short transcript of the full request (headers + body) and one raw response? We need to rule out token truncation or streaming differences. Also ask if they were hitting a dedicated vs hosted route.

acme-rep: They replied with full JSON and raw response. I'll paste the important bits: 
Request body: ```{
  "model":"redwood-v9.0",
  "input":"How do I rotate API keys for our service without causing downtime?",
  "temperature":0.1,
  "max_tokens":120
}```
Raw assistant text: "Create new key, deploy alongside old, switch traffic, revoke old."

sofia.chen: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) model policy/regression reduced verbosity for safety/conciseness at low temps, 2) token budget or stop sequence is triggering early stop. Also check if we inadvertently enabled "concise_mode" for v9.0 canary.

mike_g: I can pull the canary model config. Give me a minute.

mike_g: Config diff (v8.3 -> v9.0) excerpt: 
- default_response_style: "balanced"
+ default_response_style: "concise"
+ concise_truncation_threshold: 0.2

mike_g: Oh. That explains a lot. There was a flag flip in the rollout config. It was intended to reduce long-winded answers for some internal benchmarks but got applied broadly.

kai-h: Can we scope that flag to internal test tenants only? If it's a model config, we should revert the default for hosted customers immediately.

sofia.chen: Action items: 
- ellie_support: ask customer if they can retest against v8.3 (we can route them) and confirm differences.
- kai-h & mike_g: patch the canary config to remove default "concise" for public tenants and redeploy canary. 
- acme-rep: collect any other customer examples (short list) and send to eng-ml for analysis.

ellie_support: On it — asking customer for confirmation and offering to re-route them to v8.3 for immediate mitigation.

acme-rep: Customer accepted a reroute test. I'll update thread with v8.3 transcript when they send it.

deploy-bot: redwood-v9.0 canary config updated (reverted default_response_style) by @kai-h at 2024-11-12T20:10:23Z.

mike_g: Also logging note: add a debug flag to record "response_style" applied to each response in production logs for 24h so we can metricize impact.

sofia.chen: Agree. Kai, can you add the logging? Also add an eval against our prompt-set to measure avg token delta and helpfulness score pre/post.

kai-h: Will do. Sending PR for logging + config patch now.

acme-rep: Customer retest results: routed to v8.3, got this answer: 
```
Assistant: Rotating API keys without downtime typically involves: 1) issuing a new key and deploying it with your service while still accepting the old key, 2) gradually shifting traffic to the new key, 3) monitoring logs for auth failures, and 4) revoking the old key after verification. Here is a sample script and rollback plan...
```

acme-rep: They confirmed this matches their expectation. They said they rely on the extra detail and the friendliness tone.

sofia.chen: Great repro. Closing loop: we'll notify the customer once the canary change is rolled to prod or if we decide to keep the concise default for specific tenant profiles.

ellie_support: Customer asked for a short timeframe to see full fix. Suggested ETA: 24-48h pending canary vetting.

mike_g: I'll spike telemetry to quantify percentage of responses that shortened by >30% tokens since the v9.0 rollout window.

sofia.chen: Thanks everyone. Tagging eng-ml for model tuning follow-up. :pray:

acme-rep: Thanks — I'll update FinApps and keep this thread posted.
